The hybrid invisibility cloak integrates transparent metasurfaces and zero-index materials to function in transmission geometry.
The cloaking shell consists of a double-layer: an outer transparent metasurface and an inner zero-index material layer.
The zero-index material is realized by dielectric photonic crystals with Dirac cone dispersions at 10.2 GHz.
The metasurface is designed with ABA sandwich structures providing a linear phase shift covering [0, 2π) with high transmittance (~87%).
The experimental cloak was rhombic shaped with a side length of 234.3 mm, enclosing a metallic rhombus of 108 mm side length.
A λ/4 (wavelength quarter) distance of 10.2 GHz wave in free space separates the metallic object and the photonic crystal ZIM.
Finite element simulations show near-perfect cloaking with scattering reduced to less than 1% compared to uncloaked cases.
The cloak works for transverse electric (TE) polarization in the microwave frequency range.
Far-field radiation patterns demonstrate significant suppression of scattering in all directions with the cloak.
The metasurface imposes a phase change Δφ to match the incident wave phase to the zero-index material surface phase.
The zero-index material tunnels electromagnetic waves around the hidden region, preserving wavefront and phase.
The cloak thickness can be reduced to about 1% of the cloaked region radius, enabling ultrathin cloaks.
The cloaking effect is limited to a narrow frequency bandwidth due to phase continuity requirements.
The cloak is designed for a fixed incident angle with small angular tolerance.
The hybrid cloak principle can be extended to other zero-index materials such as metallic metamaterials and waveguides at cut-off frequencies.
The metasurface and zero-index material together overcome the reflection limitation of zero-index materials in free space.
The experimental setup used a parallel plate waveguide and a horn antenna to generate TE-polarized plane waves.
The photonic crystal ZIM consists of alumina cylinders with relative permittivity 8.1 and radius 3.95 mm arranged in a square lattice with 17.46 mm lattice constant.
The metasurface is ultrathin and modeled as an anisotropic effective medium with full phase tuning capability.
The hybrid cloak avoids the need for spatially varying extreme material parameters required by transformation optics cloaks.
